column1: # Pre-registered manifest — orchestrate-loop generalization arm, RE-RUN with a
# harness fix. Written BEFORE the first cell of this arm. Separate arm, separate
# results file; the confounded arm below is not amended or re-labeled.
# WHY A RE-RUN, NOT A CONTINUATION.
# experiment-manifest-orchestrate-userstory.tsv (results:
# experiment-results-orchestrate-userstory.tsv) was stopped early at 4 cells
# (seeds 201-204), by design, once the cause was confirmed: `runDirectiveOnce`
# built the orchestrate prompt from `task` alone, while the non-directive phase
# loop (`runOnce`, main.swift:202,390) always includes `sharedContext` (mission
# + tech-stack.md, which pins `fastapi[standard]`) in its packets. On
# `roadmap-user-story`'s business-outcome phrasing, an orchestrator given no
# framework pin built the ENTIRE APP IN FLASK, passed its own phase validation
# (which also never checks the framework), and failed the acceptance suite's
# `from app import app` at collection time — a total loss. All three graded
# cells (201 fail, 203 fail, 202 harness-void via turnDidNotEnd) trace to this;
# verified directly by recovering the leaked dispatch worktree for seed 203 and
# re-running the acceptance suite by hand: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module
# named 'flask'`. Continuing that arm to n=10 would have spent ~4 more hours
# confirming the same known bug rather than answering the generalization
# question. Stopping was an instrument-integrity call, not outcome-chasing on
# the pass rate — the stop file went in before any further cell's result was
# known.
# THE FIX (Sources/SwiftStarKit/OrchestrateDirective.swift): `build` gained an
# optional `projectContext` parameter (default "", every existing call site and
# all 8 pre-existing tests unaffected — verified, `swift test --filter
# OrchestrateDirectiveTests` 11/11 green including 3 new cases). `main.swift`'s
# directive call site now passes `sharedContext` (the same value `runOnce`
# already used). This closes the specific gap; it is not a claim that directive
# mode and phase-loop mode are now identical in every respect.
# PROVENANCE: repo HEAD (see git log at run time) + this fix, committed before
# the first cell (fix is source-only, no engine/ds4 change). ds4 pin unchanged
# from the confounded arm (1a2dddf). TURN_TIMEOUT=1500, RUN_CAP=3600 — same as
# the confounded arm, so timeout policy is not a variable between them.
# DESIGN: same task (roadmap-user-story), same n=10 as originally planned, same
# decision rule. Seeds 211-220 — disjoint from 201-210 (confounded arm), 101-130
# and 42 (roadmap-spec Block A), so no cell here was ever run under the old,
# broken prompt.
# PRIMARY ENDPOINT: pass rate on roadmap-user-story under the fixed prompt,
# Wilson 95% interval, read against Block A's roadmap-spec baseline 27/29=93%
# (still not pooled — different task, per the original design's reasoning).
# DECISION RULE, unchanged from the original design:
#  1. >=8/10 (80%): the loop generalizes across this task shift once given the
#     same project context the phase loop already gets.
#  2. 5-7/10: a real signal that task framing matters beyond the missing
#     context; underpowered to size it further at this n.
#  3. <=4/10: reliability is task-specific even with the fix; the 93% figure
#     keeps its "measured on one task" caveat, and failures feed the Backlog
#     entry directly [corrected 2026-08-29: originally "direct P27
#     inputs.
# Additionally: if ANY cell in this arm still substitutes Flask (or otherwise
# ignores the now-present project context), that is reported explicitly and
# separately from the pass rate — it would mean the fix is necessary but not
# sufficient, a different finding than "the loop doesn't generalize."
# WHAT THIS CANNOT CONCLUDE: anything about tasks other than these two; a
# precise rate at n=10; whether other gaps exist between directive mode and the
# phase loop besides the one fixed here.
# Runner: TURN_TIMEOUT=1500 RUN_CAP=3600 \
